notes.title: Steampost of Greater Updates
notes.notes:
[p][b]Progress has been great on our feature complete demo and it was high time we updated our store page description to reflect the changes we've made. We hope you'll find this exciting![/b][/p][p][/p][p]Where Birds Go To Sleep is a narrative adventure mystery game like no other - a blend of Tabletop Role-Playing Games, Point & Click Adventures and mystery games with narrative choices and world exploration.[/p][p]Slip into the mind of Cormo, a villainous pirate-turned-explorer driven by greed as he embarks on a secret mission within the prison island. The journey goes awry - Cormo is shipwrecked, and toxic, mind-numbing fog shrouds the island. [i]The prison colony is strangely quiet…[/i][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/462739981060120e64d704df7c1df01658103560.gif"][/img][/p][p]As the tower built to reach the heavens and meet God nears completion[i] - an island appears in the distant sea. Prisoners are sent to establish a colony and chart it.[/i][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/0a387984f1d53cff4eb16f4e2abc578866e5a315.png"][/img][/p][p]The whole island presents a multi-layered, interlocking mystery. Delve into the depths of the prison colony, a shifting island covered in a strange, mind-altering fog. Solve diegetic puzzles, and uncover secrets hidden around every corner. It’s up to you to find them.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/61edf466cab5fd91744aefea5bcae27af83fab2b.gif"][/img]  [/p][p][/p][p]Collect clues and use items - Secrets hide in plain sight, and you will have to use tools both mundane and cosmic to uncover them: such as a shovel or a rope, but also time, gravity, perspective, spoken clues and your own sanity.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/da0a02375fa7900271486d8716a82ab5ce04aa94.gif"][/img]  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/d99a4b64a9d0e3f203818c472b672023dc963507.png"][/img][/p][p]See the world through the eyes of a mentally and morally unstable person. Delve into difficult topics and taboos.[/p][p]On your journey you will meet a handful of developed, complex characters. Become their friend, learn their desires, and then… lie, manipulate, cheat, commit depraved acts; become what you hate; or fight against your nature. [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/379bdbfa58d62f6b4fb2eb6e08f884844ad20f0b.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/30e44d317cea7e64751c7d5794b10bbaa75c5732.png"][/img][/p][p]It’s all about awareness and knowledge. Stats and attributes may ease your journey, but they won’t solve the cosmic mysteries for you. Uncover secrets and hidden messages around every corner. Fully missable. It’s up to you to find them.[/p][p]Around us are things we don’t understand. Invisible demons, devils, coincidences, dreams and dangers unexplored.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/ebe4c01b1dd923b4b10beecd2acff60f17c8db05.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/cbe0e4c8480d73c2c49e8fa24c421ae79409e732.png"][/img][/p][p]Choices affect things big and small - a different description, a different option, a different inner world - a different Cormo, wrestling for control against [b][u]you[/u][/b]. Manipulate him into doing your bidding, break him and override his will, or cooperate and work as a team.[/p][p]The experimental [b]Heart System[/b] will re-contextualise your experience and challenge you to see things in new and exciting ways in and outside of the game as well.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/807aedc2db85c31c38d4392b7ea71560ada8c1d9.gif"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/57a638d02510b599679bcf3d5bb87d123412176f.png"][/img][/p][p]There is no golden path or fail states; every “no” or failure - and sometimes, even death - lead to new opportunities and paths to discover. What has happened cannot be undone.  [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/69afa751e4320899ece13432d50cf99928e90690.gif"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/32bd5d23255f329a9fc7ddd4925d98c7de701e53.png"][/img][/p][p]Immerse yourself in a richly detailed, fictional world inspired by the mythical Middle East, but set at the turn of the 16th century, where exotic fantasy and harsh reality meet. [/p][p]Brought to life with stunning hand painted art, stellar voice acting and atmospheric and haunting soundtrack composed and recorded in-house.[/p][p]A story spanning the entire spectrum of human emotion; trivial, humorous, disgusting, grotesque, and tragic. All at once. [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/f2645977040c8f511c228a48f6b44c2efc67f654.png"][/img][/p][p]The time for our new demo releasing is drawing ever closer. We've run a few rounds of testing on our Discord server that yielded invaluable feedback, helping us shape the game and make it better. We'd like to continue this trend, so if that's something you're interested in, join our server: https://discord.gg/YSFbT3HzrH[/p][p][url="https://discord.gg/YSFbT3HzrH" style="button"]Join our Discord![/url]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/c4b7a99d148984ee2fcc516da9f09087eaf78bb7.gif"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Steampost of Lesser Updates 2
notes.notes:
We’ve been hard at work on the game and our new feature complete demo. It’s all coming together steadily, and we thought it’s time to share some more with you:

[h2]It's not gambling - you're not playing for money. Just for your life.[/h2]
Cormo has long left behind his ruinous habit of gambling. But it's hard to lose old habits. They don't want to lose you either.

On your explorations you’ll come across dice. Cormo fidgets with them, reminiscing for a moment before tossing them. He’ll never know what he rolled… [b][u]but you will[/u][/b].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/1eaa0ad9a92fce75a90e7c530bfd6e92160fadd0.gif[/img]

Scenarios are high risk actions that can be attempted using rolled dice - or just leaving it up to luck or fate.

This might be performing an acrobatic feat, trying not to throw up, or deciding whether Cormo’s will or yours will prevail. But the most important of them all is of course - FISHING.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/de1e0a5972ebed66b4193d3626f729ea43862eb4.gif[/img]

Cormo can find fishing spots - but he never seems to catch any fish. In our game, you will fish out everything BUT fish - from utensils to old memorabilia. But don’t be sad, these items can be repurposed as [b][u]gifts you can give to other characters[/u][/b], but more on that in a later update.

[h2]Constellations of the Mind[/h2]
Where Birds Go to Sleep features “knowledge puzzles” akin to those in Outer Wilds; puzzles you might not even realise are there at first, and once you know the solution to them, you can solve them within minutes.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/d66722b35e7c10cc6c9920c22a1d13fa707257f6.gif[/img]

As you explore, you will come across clues to puzzles that will be collected into your Mindmap in the form of clue cards. The Mindmap screen is like a quest log, and it is an essential part of the experience.

[h2]A Tapestry Within[/h2]
Almost every dialogue choice in the game subtly changes Cormo’s personality. The personality stats you get from choices were previously not shown anywhere at all, causing a lot of confusion as to what choices really did. Later, we created a section for them in the Inventory but it felt a bit too cramped. Now, stats have their own screen with flashy artwork and animations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/175f33761e84317c39ce7fb15b9ccf7982681fbf.gif[/img]

The stats affect things big and small - a different description, a different option, a different inner world - a different Cormo, wrestling for control against you based on these stats.

[h2]Chart the Unknown[/h2]
In a few of our previous news posts, you could get a glimpse of our exploration mechanics and the map. In our next update, we’ll show more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/7e2e8a6701590012028c1a3eef28e9b655892157.png[/img]

[h2]Help us make the game better![/h2]
The time for our new demo releasing is drawing ever closer. We've run a few rounds of testing on our Discord server that yielded invaluable feedback, helping us shape the game and make it better. We'd like to continue this trend, so if that's something you're interested in, join our server for when the new testing call opens: https://discord.gg/YSFbT3HzrH

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/c4b7a99d148984ee2fcc516da9f09087eaf78bb7.gif[/img]

notes.title: Steampost of Lesser Updates
notes.notes:
Sorry for the long radio silence. We have been working hard on the game and made some really great progress. We're still working on our feature complete demo and have been prototyping different maps.

Here are a couple of things we've already implemented:

[h2]Inventory and Stats[/h2]
If you have played our public demo, you'll remember the “Mindmap” screen, which was accessed by pressing “M” contained ideas about everything - the quests, the items you carry and lore.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/41a5d1f67e9ba3b7d2664b94835d8c5f04378245.gif[/img]

The Mindmap has been separated into more traditional categories. The first is the [b]inventory[/b] which allows you to browse, inspect, equip and use your collected items. Your accrued character traits were hidden in the previous demo, but now the system is transparent and you will be able keep track of them.

There’s also Thoughts, Clues and Nighthawks, we’ll keep those for another update.



[h2]Further UI Redesigns and Polish[/h2]
We have been hard at work on a big UI overhaul, polish and quality of life improvements. We want to save some of the bigger ones for the next update.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/fc693fd3bd96f14cd2c3d4a31bc7e72f82e7fdcb.gif[/img]
New items get marked in the inventory by a dot on the tab it's in, and get a sheen to signal they're new.


[h2]Narrative Log & Dialogue Skipping[/h2]
Due to popular demand, we have implemented a narrative log. You'll be able to summon it during dialogues to see what has been said, and the options you have chosen.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/82e714e62e56126c9f846aa2cb6868372116819b.png[/img]

Another very sought after feature - “dialogue skipping” has been in the plans forever but originally we only wanted to enable it if you were replaying the game - this is not the case anymore, it'll be available from the get-go.

When you press "cancel" (ie "B" on an xbox controller), a text popup will appear on the bottom of your screen telling you to press it again to skip, to prevent you from accidentally skipping.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/d65b32e5d115834f41acdbb5e793086e4af59216.png[/img]

[table noborder=1 equalcells=1]
    [tr]
        [th][h2]Day/Night Cycle[/h2][/th]
        [th][/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td]We have not mentioned this in the past, but the game features a day/night cycle!

Actually, it’s more of a morning/dusk/midnight cycle.

The three different daytime states make different areas accessible, they are used in various puzzles and give the world a different look. 
[/td]
        [td]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/6439fc68cffa608f8f4c9c66a805e193f625c14d.gif[/img][/td]
    [/tr]
[/table] 



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/7e2e8a6701590012028c1a3eef28e9b655892157.png[/img]



Feedback is super important to us, and we're looking forward to releasing our feature complete demo into the wild to see what you all have to say about it!

[i]And last but not least… FISHING. Yes, you can fish in the game. Look out for the next update to keep up with Cormo’s angling escapades.[/i]

notes.title: Storyteller's Festival & Public Demo!
notes.notes:
We are super excited to say that Where Birds Go to Sleep is going to be part of The Storyteller's Festival!

------------------------

(Apologies for the repost - apparently the date of the broadcast was entered wrong, and Steam won't let me edit the start time!)

[h2][b][u]When:[/u][/b][/h2]
AEDT: 9:00 AM 2023 March 26
PST: 2:00 PM 2023 March 25
CET: 11:00 PM 2023 March 25


[h2][b][u]What:[/u][/b][/h2]
Our demo will be publicly available again!
For those of you who have played it last year in August or November, unfortunately this is the exact same demo, however, 

[h1]there might be some content still that you haven't seen yet:[/h1]

[h2]1. There's a big secret in our demo that we hid too well![/h2]
We learned such a big lesson with this one! Here's how to access it;
1. Sit on the bed in the tent where you can sleep
2. Open the mindmap by pressing "M" or the "options" key on your gamepad
3. Read the "Shireen's Locket" item description
4. Go straight to sleep!


[h2]2. And about those achievements...[/h2]
The demo has 13 achievements, some of which you will have to replay the demo for. Here's some of the more obscure ones:
[list]
[*] [b]Locked Locket[/b] - see the big secret above!
[*] [b]Homunculus[/b] - during the boat ride, select the second option, then when confronting Dunlin, choose to pursue the accusation.
[*] [b]Naivete[/b] - during the boat ride, select the option to tell Dunlin the joke, then during the confrontation, press him about what you saw.
[*] [b]Cowardice[/b] - at the start of the Dunlin confrontation, choose to chicken out and not tell Dunlin anything at all.
[/list]

As you can see there are multiple outcomes from the Dunlin confrontation, and they all have a different introspection scene afterwards. There are also three endings:

[h2]3. Replayabillity and endings[/h2]
We consider the demo to have two kinds of endings;

[h3]The outcome of the Dunlin conversation (of which there is 4):[/h3]
Depending on which option you choose at the start, Dunlin will either hate you or like you (this is expanded on a lot more in the final game!), and you will get a different attitude and reaction from him both in his exhausted dialogue and during the confrontation. See the achievements above on how to get the different outcomes from that conversation!

[h3]The end screen you get when you enter the forest:[/h3]
These are different based on how many secrets you found.
[list]
[*] [b]Bliss[/b] - finish the demo with no secrets found at all (essentially just speedrun it and only interact with the "main story")
[*] [b]Schizotypy[/b] - finish the demo with more than one secret found but not all
[*] [b]No More Secrets[/b] - finish the demo with all secrets found: bonfire & Colonised Brain dream ("Think about the colonists"), shoes & Generous Envoy dream ("The shoes were so small"), clicking "Notice" after the bonfire section, having dreamt the secret dream (see above!)
[/list]

Technically these can be obtained on the same save file, since you can reload your save, and interact with the content before going into the forest again.

--------------------------------------

Last but not least, we will also be running [url=https://www.youtube.com/@Dustflower]Dustflower[/url]'s playthrough as broadcast during the event on our Steam page.

In the meanwhile we're working on a feature complete demo in the meanwhile that we hope to take to Next Fest when it's ready!

Most importantly, have fun playing demos during the event!

notes.title: A Thank You, and Demo Available until 14th August
notes.notes:
Tiny Teams has wrapped a few days ago and we we would like to thank everyone who played the demo. The feedback we have received via the feedback form, Steam Discussion forums or on our Discord has been incredibly useful, and we have tried to be responsive and some reactionary changes made it into demo updates.

For the time being, we will first hide the demo for an unspecified amount of time on the 14th of August. This means that even if you have the demo in your library or installed, you will be able to run it, but new players will not be able to download it. At a later point, we will disable it fully, so you won't be able to run it. We will announce this in advance. Don't worry, the demo will be back (with some updates) later!

Thank you once again, and we are excited for the next time the demo will be public again, and for your feedback!

notes.title: Big Demo Update and Tiny Teams
notes.notes:
We are very excited to say that we're participating in TinyTeams 2022, and that our demo will be available again from the 1st of August until an unspecified date (at least until the 8th).

If you have the demo in your Steam library already, you'll already see an update for the demo - the build will have "0.71" (or higher) on the top left corner. If you don't, you will be able to access the demo again on the 1st of August!

We would love to hear your thoughts on the changes and the new content, and if you run into any issues!

[u][b]Changes:[/b][/u]
- New endscreen that shows your path taken in the demo
- A new dialogue path for the argument with Dunlin
- Shireen's Locket dream made more apparent
- WASD/Gamepad support!!
- A lot of voice lines have been cut up to be shorter so dialogue is quicker (more like movie subtitles)
- Resolutions now wont list every resolution under the sun, just the relevant ones
- Mindmap notifcation reworked, now hopefully more obvious
- Ability to dream on before waking up

notes.title: A Holistic View of Story (in Video Games)
notes.notes:
[i]This is a shortened version of one of our articles, you can read the full, unshortened version [url=https://www.wherebirdsgotosleep.com/a-holistic-view-of-story-in-video-games/]here[/url].[/i]

There is something very curious and special happening when we [b][u]interpret[/u][/b] a story. For the remainder of this article, please accept that “story” is much more than a summary of events, it is the [b][u]rhythm of life[/u][/b] as humans see it – a beginning and an end. 

We have an innate understanding of story from early childhood, which we acquire from observing life. Despite sounding very lofty and philosophical, this is a very grounded and pragmatic view. 

The story in video games is not in audio logs, cutscenes, phone-calls or never-ending text dumps of exhaustive codexes. It happens in the player’s head, where he [b][u]interprets[/u][/b] and abstracts, along with his moment-to-moment decisions and emotions. 

It is also not only the “plot”, it is also the [b][u]tempo[/u][/b], the [b][u]rhythm[/u][/b], the [b][u]speed[/u][/b], the [b][u]emotions[/u][/b] as well as the [b][u]gameplay[/u][/b]. 

So many video games have their video and game parts undermining each other at every opportunity: a character might have an emotional breakdown after killing a person in a cutscene, even though the player has killed dozens already in their current play session - the game asks us to kindly ignore the [b][u]game[/u][/b] part, which is the only part separating the game from a movie, and to focus on the [b][u]video[/u][/b] part, while the “story” takes place.

The video part of a video game can have an excellent story with great dialogues, graphics and camerawork. The gameplay might make the player enraged, stressed, exhausted, horrified or satisfied. But unless these elements work in tandem, conjoined in the player’s brain, video games cannot tell a story [b][u]unique to its medium[/u][/b].

We wouldn’t call a video which would consist of scrolling text a good movie to watch, no matter how good a story the text would tell.

We wouldn’t call a book filled with musical notes a good book to read, even though the music it describes might sound heavenly when played.

The story in the video part of a game might be great, the game’s gameplay might be fantastic, but that’s simply a good video and a good game – not a good video game.

notes.title: Introducing Our Characters
notes.notes:
In Where Birds Go To Sleep, you inhabit the unconscious mind of Cormo, a churlish sailor-turned-smuggler. To find a cure for your sister’s sickness, you sneak your way into a dangerous expedition to explore the unknown, reserved only for the worst prisoners. There, you will get to know a handful of very special, deeply developed and fully realised characters. Become their friend, get to know their secrets, manipulate or abuse them to your, or Cormo’s will.

One of the first characters you will meet is Dunlin – a noble-born, young man who is steadfast in his moral and religious principles. But what must a purebred like him be guilty of to end up here with you?

[i]“Some people copulate like animals, bolstering their sub-par breed. One such child was given up by his mother at an age older than usual. He treasured the memory of her face. He dreamt of her, of her soft hands caressing his hair.

But Cormo told no one.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/2f3d4c59b0aa46ed6e23ea5f63783efa1341fc95.jpg[/img]

[i]“Dunlin, like other distinguished, properly born males, have their likeness painted just before reaching maturity as a reference for comparison of physical features when children of lesser breed are selected to join them in pursuit of that which is noble.”[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38458508/2bfcddae4c92cf61ad1c017c01a8f214a259ac0d.jpg[/img]

notes.title: How We Make Choices Matter
notes.notes:
We make choices matter by tracking a lot of choices the player makes:

♦ We have a bunch of hidden stats in the game that track your playstyle, and every single choice affects these, tipping the scales ever so slightly each time
♦ We also track a massive amount of events and decisions specifically
♦ We have “skills” – these are passive “abilities” that are unlocked by playing a certain way. Sort of like habits.
♦ A lot of choices and actions have “hidden stat”/event/skill requirements, which if you don’t meet, you’ll still see them but wont be able to select them

For example, in a hypothetical scenario, a hidden stat could be how much a character you’re talking to, including the protagonist, likes you. If you anger him enough, maybe it’ll erupt into an argument. At this point we would take note of this, so that any future interactions with him will reflect this.

If you do a type of action for it to become habitual, you might get a skill that reflects this, which would make certain future dialogue or action choices available (or others unavailable).

Note that this does not only affect dialogue choices, but also actions you can perform elsewhere in the game.

Every single small choice you make builds up, and shifts the direction of the story. While there are crucial moments and big decisions to be made, they happen within the context of the numerous smaller decisions, even those as trivial as the way you greet someone, that – true to life – ultimately decide who we are.
